weak_supervision_note: weak_pseudo_label_positive_rate and all *_pseudo_labels agreement/precision/recall figures are WEAK SUPERVISION heuristics compared against a deterministic rule-based score, NOT real fraud ground truth -- no authoritative fraud labels were provided in the supplied data.
known_limitation: The fine-tuned model over-predicts fraud relative to the weak-label training signal (predicted positive rate 58.8% vs. weak-label rate 8.7%; precision vs. weak labels only 0.118, recall 0.805). Fine-tuning did measurably reduce the bias present in the base model zero-shot (predicted positive rate dropped from 90.8% to 58.8%), but 10 LoRA training steps on 80 examples (sized to fit a 4GB laptop GPU within a practical time budget) was not enough to fully correct a <3B model's strong prior toward flagging transactions as fraudulent. This is reported plainly as a genuine limitation rather than omitted; more training data/epochs would likely improve precision further.
